questions: Can a cake appear in more than one pair across different test cases?
Is it allowed for the same cake to be paired with itself (i.e., can a_i = b_i)?
What is the exact definition of "distinct integers" in the context of choosing a_1, b_1, ..., a_K, b_K?
Are the values of X_i, Y_i, Z_i guaranteed to fit within standard integer types (e.g., 64-bit signed integers)?
Does the phrase "greatest value among P,Q,R" imply that ties are broken arbitrarily or by some specific rule?
Must all N cakes be used in forming pairs, or can some remain unpaired?
Is there any constraint preventing multiple test cases from having overlapping N and K values?
How should the program handle cases where K=0, if such inputs are possible?
answers: Each cake can be used in at most one pair; pairs must be formed from distinct cakes without overlaps.

inline_prompts:
Takahashi, a patissier working at the ABC pastry shop, decided to sell assorted cakes to commemorate AtCoder Beginner Contest 400.
The shop sells N kinds of cakes: cake 1, cake 2, \ldots, cake N.
Each cake has three non-negative integer values: beauty, tastiness, and popularity. Specifically, cake i has beauty X_i, tastiness Y_i, and popularity Z_i.
He considers pairing up these cakes into K pairs.
Formally, he will choose 2K distinct integers a_1,b_1,a_2,b_2,\ldots,a_K,b_K between 1 and N (inclusive), and pair cake a_i with cake b_i. Each cake can be used in at most one pair; pairs must be formed from distinct cakes without overlaps.
The price of a pair formed by cakes a_i and b_i is \max(X_{a_i} + X_{b_i},\, Y_{a_i} + Y_{b_i},\, Z_{a_i} + Z_{b_i}).
Here, \max(P,Q,R) denotes the greatest value among P,Q,R.
Find the maximum possible total price of the K pairs.
You are given T test cases; solve each of them.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
T
\mathrm{case}_1
\mathrm{case}_2
\vdots
\mathrm{case}_T
\mathrm{case}_i represents the i-th test case. Each test case is given in the following format:
N K
X_1 Y_1 Z_1
X_2 Y_2 Z_2
\vdots
X_N Y_N Z_N
Output
Print the result.
Constraints
- 1\leq T\leq 1000
- 2\leq N \leq 10^5
- The sum of N over all test cases in each input file is at most 10^5.
- 1\leq K \leq \lfloor \frac{N}{2}\rfloor (For a real number x, \lfloor x\rfloor denotes the greatest integer not exceeding x.)
- 0\leq X_i,Y_i,Z_i \leq 10^9
- All input values are integers.
